chunks: Some Baghdadis wrote to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Thānī عليه السلام, asking him about going out on a Wednesday that does not rotate.

So he عليه السلام wrote: “Whoever goes out on a Wednesday that does not rotate, in مخالفة to the people of bad omens, will be protected from every harm, cured of every affliction, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will fulfill his need.”

key_terms.الطِّيَرَةِ: belief in bad omens or superstition
key_terms.الْخُرُوجِ: going out or departing, especially for travel
key_terms.لَا يَدُورُ: a specific Wednesday described as not rotating

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ḥasan al-Thānī عليه السلام say about traveling on a Wednesday considered unlucky?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the belief in ill omens associated with a particular Wednesday and instructs acting contrary to superstitious notions. It promises divine protection, well-being, and fulfillment of needs for the one who departs on that day in opposition to such beliefs.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2393 - Some Baghdadis wrote to Imam al-Hassan al-Thani (as) asking about traveling on a Wednesday that does not rotate.

Imam (as) replied: "Whoever departs on a Wednesday that does not rotate, in opposition to those who believe in bad omens, will be protected from all harm, healed from every affliction, and Allah (swt), the Exalted, will fulfill his need."
